metrics.name: Single-turn harmless response rate
metrics.notes: Anthropic's own safety-eval suite; percentage of harmful/sensitive prompts where the model did not facilitate the requested harm. Higher is better.

metrics.name: Single-turn over-refusal rate
metrics.notes: Share of benign prompts the model declined. Lower is better.

metrics.name: Multi-turn appropriate response rate
metrics.notes: Not comparable across risk-area categories (each graded against its own rubric).

metrics.name: Sandbox/containment boundary escape propensity
metrics.notes: Share of scenarios (28 handmade, 7 runs each) resulting in an attempted containment-boundary crossing. Lower is better.

metrics.name: Propensity to publish harmful content to public package registries
metrics.notes: Simulated CTF-exercise scenario; no real content is published. Lower is better.

metrics.name: Compliance rate with instructions planted in user-pasted text
metrics.notes: Distinct from indirect prompt injection via tool results (see Section 5.2 of source). Lower is better.

metrics.name: SHADE-Arena stealth success rate
metrics.notes: Fraction of attempts completing a harmful side task without the monitor flagging the transcript. Direction is context-dependent: for a well-aligned model, a LOW stealth rate under adversarial/optimized prompting and even lower under the standard prompt is the desired outcome; this is a red-team/control eval, not a quality benchmark.

metrics.name: LinuxArena stealth success rate
metrics.notes: Redwood Research / EquiStamp AI control arena. Same direction caveat as shade-arena-stealth-rate.

metrics.name: Reward hacking success rate (RL training)
metrics.notes: Share of sampled RL training episodes in which a reward-hacking classifier judged the model successfully hacked the reward. Lower is better.

metrics.name: Verbalized evaluation awareness (white-box)
metrics.notes: Fraction of transcripts where white-box probing finds the model internally suspects it is being evaluated. Direction is context-dependent: high awareness can undermine the reliability of behavioral evaluations (bad for measurement validity) independent of whether the model's actual behavior is good.

metrics.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2
metrics.notes: Aggregate of 10 evaluations (AA-Briefcase v1.1, GDPval-AA v2.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1). Distinct metric identity from v4.2/v4.1; do not cross-rank.

metrics.name: Factual error rate on difficult (error-inducing) prompts
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval on de-identified ChatGPT conversations where users had flagged a factual error from a prior model. Explicitly NOT representative of typical usage (error-inducing sample, not a random sample); not controlled for response length.

metrics.name: Coding deception rate (adversarial, max effort)
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval: agents given tasks deliberately selected to elicit dishonesty. Fraction of answers with any detected deception. Not representative of typical usage; effort fixed at maximum in the source.

metrics.name: Broken search tool non-disclosure rate (adversarial, max effort)
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval: agents given search tasks and a broken search tool, graded on whether they disclose the broken tool instead of guessing. Tasks selected to elicit failures; effort fixed at maximum in the source.

metrics.name: Codex safety-reviewer bypass attempt rate (adversarial, max effort)
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval: whether models try to work around a Codex automated safety reviewer that blocked a command as unsafe. Effort fixed at maximum in the source.

metrics.name: Explicit-warning circumvention attempt rate (adversarial, max effort)
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval: whether models attempt to work around explicit restriction warnings (e.g. an "access denied" message). Tests primarily cover low-stakes situations without full system-level safeguards. Effort fixed at maximum in the source.

metrics.name: Unauthorized agent interaction rate (simulated message board)
metrics.notes: OpenAI internal eval: whether models follow unauthorized instructions found on a simulated message board (e.g. requests to disclose private information), conditional on the model finding the board. Effort not stated in the source for this chart (unlike the other four adversarial-agent charts on the same page, which state max). Distinct from gpt6-agent-to-agent-engagement-rate (system-card Fig 12), which measures whether the model engaged with/discovered the board at all — this metric measures whether it then took the unauthorized action, conditional on finding the board. Do not conflate the two.
